A lightning strike caused delamination on the LE flange, potentially affecting all layers. This increases the risk of critical failure if left unrepaired. Delaying the repair will likely worsen the delamination and cause cracks. An LPS inspection is required. Internal access isn't possible, the alternative repair involves cutting out the affected area from the outside, laminating and applying a hardback, applying bonding paste for a smooth profile, laminating new inner shell layers, and laminating outer shell layers with reinforcement. The repair plan requires engineer approval. This repair should be completed as soon as possible because the Lightning Protection System (LPS) might be compromised. After the repair, repeat the LPS inspection.

A lightning strike caused delamination. This can lead to a higher risk of critical failure if it continues to grow. Delaying repair will likely worsen the delamination and potentially cause cracks. The repair process involves rebuilding the shear web flange, grinding out affected inner shell layers, inspecting and potentially regrinding the glue line, inspecting the main girder (proceed only if undamaged), inspecting and replacing core material if needed, applying a smooth radius of bonding paste to the corner between web and shell, laminating new inner shell layers, and reinforcing with an overlap of the shear web flange. This repair should be done as soon as possible. If delayed, the next internal inspection must be conducted within 3 months.
